title: Dedicated cluster: burst-policy calibration, tenant isolation tags, and reservation autosizing follow-up
creator: Amina Patel
description: Summary: During a peak on 2026-03-08 we observed repeated QoS regressions across three dedicated clusters. Root cause analysis shows a combination of under-provisioned tenant reservations, a burst-token decay that was too permissive for small noisy tenants, and an admission path that let long-running batched jobs acquire burst tokens without accounting for request tail latencies. Impact: several customers experienced transient 500s and elevated latency that breached SLOs for the cluster-tiered SLA. Outage window: 2026-03-08 02:12 UTC to 2026-03-08 05:40 UTC. Detection: alerting on eviction rate and p99 latency triggered first; on-call correlation with recent reservation resize API calls highlighted a tenant that had reduced reservation by 40% the prior day. Root cause details: (1) Reservation autosizer used a 7-day median rather than a 30-day weighted median, which under-estimated burst patterns for tenants with weekly spikes. (2) Burst token bucket had a half-life of 15 minutes, allowing burst tokens to accumulate for noisy tenants across short gaps; combined with scheduler packing it led to burst saturation. (3) Admission controller did not gate batched throughput for tenants with low reservation: long batched queries consumed burst tokens and prevented other tenants from getting low-latency scheduling slots. Goals for follow-up: automated detection of reservation under-sizing regressions, recalibration of burst decay and token gain to reflect tenant variance and instance density, tenant-scoped isolation tags to prevent noisy tenant displacement, and an admission control change to deprioritize long batched requests when cluster burst utilization is above threshold.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Amina: Initial postmortem draft attached, linked timeline to snapshots and alert logs. Noted the autosizer config used the 7-day median. Filing follow-ups for autosizer and burst policy.

2026-03-11 - Marco: Reproduced token-bucket saturation in simulator with 12 tenants; provided a synthetic load repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-sim/tree/ENG-41322 . Opening spike-test PR shortly.

2026-03-12 - Priya (SRE): Deployed temporary mitigation: per-tenant burst cap at 2x reservation and admission gate for batched jobs; reduced customer impact during evening peak. Observability dashboards updated: added 'burst-utilization-by-tenant' and 'reservation-variance' panels.
2026-03-13 - Design review (Ravi): Agreed that UI needs a reservation health panel; PM to own product change. Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Reservation+Health+UX (draft).
2026-03-14 - Marco: Running canary for new admission gate in dedicated-canary-3; no regressions so far. Scheduling a review with runtime team for kernel-level preemption behavior.
Runbook changes will be captured in: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Dedicated+Burst+Mitigations
action_items: Autosizer: change heuristic to 30-day weighted median and add outlier detection; owner: Marco; ETA: 2026-03-21
Burst policy: reduce token half-life from 15m to 6m and enforce per-tenant burst cap of 2x reservation; owner: Priya; ETA: 2026-03-18
Admission controller: implement 'batch-deprioritization' when cluster burst-utilization > 60%; owner: Julio; ETA: 2026-03-25
Tenant isolation: add tenant isolation tag and scheduler soft-anti-affinity to spread suspected noisy tenants; owner: Sched Team; ETA: 2026-04-04
Observability: add regression alert on 'reservation-to-traffic-ratio' dropping below 0.6 for >30m; owner: SRE; ETA: 2026-03-16
UX: Reservation health panel and contextual guidance for resizing; owner: Priya (PM) and Ravi (Design); ETA: 2026-04-01
acceptance_criteria: Autosizer produces different recommended reservation for impacted tenants in retrospective simulation and reduces under-provisioned recommendations by >=20% compared to current algorithm
Burst policy change verified in simulator with 100 synthetic tenants showing 30% reduction in tenant eviction incidents at 99th percentile
Admission controller change prevents long batched jobs from consuming burst tokens during sustained cluster-wide spikes with no customer-facing SLO regressions
New dashboard panels show tenant-level burst utilization and send alerts when threshold breached
notes: Trade-off: shorter token half-life reduces short-term developer throughput for bursty but well-behaved tenants; we mitigate via UX guidance and a temporary grace period for customers flagged as high-trust
We considered hard cgroup-based throttling but deferred to soft-deprioritization to avoid unsafe preemption of critical long-running inferences
Implementation plan favors a simulator-first approach: validate configuration changes in cluster-sim, run dedicated canary, then roll with feature-flag across clusters
